root_cause.text: The `ip6_err_gen_icmpv6_unreach()` function clones an outer IPv4 ICMP error packet and reuses its control buffer (`cb`) without zeroing it, causing the IPv4 `inet_skb_parm` (including an attacker-controlled CIPSO offset) to be misinterpreted as the IPv6 `inet6_skb_parm` (specifically the `dsthao` field), leading to an unchecked offset used in `mip6_addr_swap()` that can result in an out-of-bounds read/write.
root_cause.evidence: The patch clears the control buffer with `memset(IP6CB(skb2), 0, sizeof(*IP6CB(skb2)));`. The CVE description explains the exact overlap: "The cipso offset in inet_skb_parm.opt directly overlaps with dsthao in inet6_skb_parm at offset 18" and that "If an attacker sends a forged ICMPv4 error with a CIPSO IP option, dsthao would be a non-zero offset. ... Could mip6_addr_swap() then perform a 16-byte swap that extends past the end of the packet data into skb_shared_info?"

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove residual IPv4 stack data from the IPv6 control block to prevent incorrect behavior in ICMPv6 unreachable generation.
intent_record.what: Added a call to memset to zero out the IP6CB control block of skb2 after its allocation.
intent_record.how: This ensures that any leftover data from the IPv4 stack (which may have previously processed the socket buffer) is cleared, avoiding potential misinterpretation of control information when generating an ICMPv6 unreachable message.
